In [[American football]], an [[interception]] (INT), also known as a pick, occurs when a [[Forward pass|pass]] intended for a player of the same team is caught by an opposition player, who then gains possession for their team.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023 NFL Rulebook |url=https://operations.nfl.com/the-rules/nfl-rulebook/ |website=[[National Football League]] |access-date=November 6, 2023 |archive-date=October 24, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231024215328/https://operations.nfl.com/the-rules/nfl-rulebook/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Football Interceptions |url=https://www.rookieroad.com/football/glossary-of-terms/interceptions/ |website=Rookie Road |access-date=November 6, 2023 |language=en |archive-date=August 18, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230818231129/https://www.rookieroad.com/football/glossary-of-terms/interceptions/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[National Football League]] (NFL) did not begin keeping official records until the 1932 season and did not begin tracking interceptions until 1940.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL's Passer Rating |url=http://www.profootballhof.com/history/release.aspx?release_id=1303 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003213325/http://www.profootballhof.com/history/release.aspx?release_id=1303 |archive-date=October 3, 2015 |access-date=June 19, 2013 |website=[[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Football Statistics Data Coverage |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/about/coverage.htm |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |access-date=November 6, 2023 |language=en |archive-date=May 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230516221758/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/about/coverage.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> As a result of the [[AFL–NFL merger]], league record books also recognize statistics from the [[American Football League]] (AFL), which operated from 1960 to 1969 before being absorbed into the NFL in 1970.<ref name="Yearly Statistical Leaders">{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Record and Fact Book |url=http://static.nfl.com/static/content/public/image/history/pdfs/Records/Yrly_Stat_Ld_2011.pdf |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120913213850/http://static.nfl.com/static/content/public/image/history/pdfs/Records/Yrly_Stat_Ld_2011.pdf |archive-date=September 13, 2012 |access-date=June 19, 2013 |website=[[National Football League]] |pages=625–626 }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Banks |first1=Don |title=Forty-five years after last AFL season, rivalry with NFL still resonates |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2014/11/12/afl-history-kansas-city-chiefs-oakland-raiders |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=October 12, 2023 |language=en-us |date=November 12, 2014 |archive-date=December 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221227010716/http://www.si.com/nfl/2014/11/12/afl-history-kansas-city-chiefs-oakland-raiders |url-status=live }}</ref>

There have been 39 players who have recorded at least 50 interceptions. [[Paul Krause]] is the all-time leader, with 81 interceptions.<ref name=Jones/> Due to rule changes and increasingly detailed offensive schemes, among other factors, the rate of interceptions has dropped considerably from 1971 (5.78%) to 2018 (2.37%).<ref name=Jones>{{cite magazine|last=Jones|first=Jonathan|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2019/10/02/nfl-interception-rate-decline|title=The Declining Interception Rate in the NFL|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=October 2, 2019|accessdate=October 1, 2024|archive-date=June 23, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240623182006/https://www.si.com/nfl/2019/10/02/nfl-interception-rate-decline|url-status=live}}</ref> As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, [[Harrison Smith]] is the only active player that has at least 40 interceptions.
